pr_title: Fix ONVIF config entry unique ID
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Fixes issue where some ONVIF devices do not expose MAC address through the API.  This falls back to the serial number as the config entry Unique ID, fixing #35883

While testing (adding and removing config entries after commenting out portions of code) I realized that the Event subscription is not ended properly when removing a config entry and will continue attempting to poll the device indefinitely until a Home Assistant reboot.  A fix for that is also included in this PR.

While playing around in config flow, I also made password optional which fixes #35904

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
It is not possible to integrate my ONVIF camera that requires an empty password.
The onvif yaml config is no more documented, so the onvif integration setup wizard from Lovelace should add support for this.
Also, the newly ONVIF dicovered integration can't be "ignored".

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->
Home assistant on Raspberry Pi4.

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.110
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Home Assistant
- Integration causing this issue: onvif
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/onvif/

comments:
Hey there @hunterjm, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`onvif`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L289) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

ONVIF doesn't have a discovery flow, so it shouldn't show up with either "Configure" or "Ignore" buttons.  You have to manually add it.  Will look into allowing empty passwords... but that just sounds really bad.  Are you sure your camera doesn't allow you to set one?

What is the Make/Model of the device?

The device is a Xiaovv Q8 HD 1080P 360°: it is a cheap camera that supports ONVIF with PTZ, but doesn't allow to change the password (empty) for the only user ("admin") authorized on the onvif interface. The only password you can set and change is that of their cloud platform and app, but it is not used for onvif. I tested it successfully with other generic onvif clients that support empty passwords.
Thank you!

@hunterjm  Some budget IP cameras such as Digoo do not use a password "out of the box" and in fact the only way to update the password is to reflash the units with custom code.  Agreed not a purchase of choice but in some countries the range of decent, budget ONVIF cameras is very limited

review_comments: We don't need both connections and identifiers. One is enough.
There won't be any MAC for #35883, which is why I added identifiers back in.   What would be the better way to handle this?  Have two conditionals to add either/or?

If we would be sure that serial number is always available it would be enough with that identifier.

Otherwise, I think this is ok. But please add a comment why it's here since it's not in line with our standard.

Even if I could guarantee the `SerialNumber` would always be populated and unique but sometimes I could also retrive a `MAC` from the device, I would still want to include the MAC address.  This way, the device registry can link devices from multiple integrations together.  The perfect example of this is how this ONVIF device merges with a device registry entry created by the UniFi integration.  This allows me to see all related entities together.

On a side note, you can find an example of both being populated in the developer documentation here: https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/device_registry_index/#defining-devices

The above can be a different conversation, however.  I've modified the code to reflect the uncertainty that serial number will always exist, but due to config flow constraints there will be at least one of the two.  I also added a detailed comment in the code.
Is it the case that some cameras have mac address but not serial number and some cameras have serial number but not mac address?

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/35883#issuecomment-631930309 shows that some cameras don't return a MAC, but do return a SerialNumber.  I do not know of any cases where no serial number is returned, but wouldn't be surprised if there is one somewhere...

Edit: "Device ID" in the screenshot on this comment is what ONVIF Device Manager (3rd party program) populates from `SerialNumber` in the API.

The real reason for this statement is backwards compatibility for entities.  MAC was pulled and used as `unique_id` between my time working on this integration.  This way will only break entity mapping for devices that don't return a MAC, which are already currently completely broken, so not a huge deal breaker.
